newsitem.title: USA: ADL protests AOL's KKK site.
newsitem.headline: ADL protests AOL's KKK site.

text.p: The Anti-Defamation League criticised America Online Wednesday for continuing to allow an Internet site that supports and urges membership in the Ku Klux Klan.

"Our concern is that hate that was once local is now global," Lauren Levin, a lawyer with the Anti-Defamation League's Boston office. "America Online has established as their own standards under which they would remove language which they consider harmful or offensive.
"And it is the Anti-Defamation League's concern that by America Online allowing this Klan site to disseminate its messages, they are saying there is nothing offensive about the site," Levin said.
America Online spokeswoman Wendy Goldberg said the Virginia-based Internet provider, which claims 8 million subscribers, has been in contact with the ADL.
"And we obviously agree that what the KKK represents is reprehensible. For the time being the KKK site is historical in character, but we will be monitoring the situation very carefully."
Earlier this week AOL closed down a different KKK site that the company felt was "inciteful and provocative," she said.
